newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Benelux bourses talking about cross-membership.
newsitem.headline: Benelux bourses talking about cross-membership.

text.p: The three Benelux bourses - Brussels, Amsterdam and Luxembourg -- are in talks about how to facilitate cross-membership, Boudewijn van Ittersum, the outgoing chairman of the newly united Amsterdam Exchanges said on Thursday.

"Members in Brussels would have direct access to Amsterdam and Luxembourg and vice versa," van Ittersum told Reuters at a seminar on stock markets and economic and monetary union (EMU) organised by the British Chamber of Commerce.
He said the talks were mainly focused on technological issues, such as how the bourses could share data feeds to enable price information to be simultaneously displayed in the three centres.
The Brussels and Luxembourg stock exchanges said earlier this year they were holding talks, but at that stage the Amsterdam bourse's involvement was not made public.
Van Ittersum told the seminar he expected that stock exchanges in distinct economic regions in Europe, such as the Benelux and Scandinavia, would cooperate more closely once EMU starts.

He said he also expected the Euro.NM initiative, which will eventually create a common technological platform for trading small company stocks between the Paris, Brussels, Amsterdam and Frankfurt bourses, could become "a nucleus of a new approach towards regulated market integration in Europe."

"Within a successful EMU, this approach could result in an easily acceptable network for trading and settlement, linking the national exchanges. I expect this to be the realistic way to overcome the present market fragmentation of Europe over the next 10 to 20 years," van Ittersum, a former President of the European Federation of Stock Exchanges, said.
"I expect the Euro.NM to develop into a much more comprehensive structure which can be used for other market segments, not only new companies as it is used today," he said
This would allow the bourses to develop new products tailored to EMU without forcing them to change their existing practices.

Marc-Antoine de Schoutheete, head of corporate finance at Belgium's Generale Bank, said he too believed the Euro.NM, despite its slow start, would prove successful. He noted that there were rumours the Vienna and Madrid stock exchanges were also interested in the project.
